en.heading: ## [Unreleased]
en.body:
### Added

- Device-code login (for example GitHub Copilot) now opens the verification page and copies the code when you press Enter. Providers can turn either action off with `openBrowserOnConfirm: false` or `copyCodeOnConfirm: false` ([#9282](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9282), [#9301](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9301))

### Changed

- `pi update` for installs from the pi.dev installer no longer passes `--min-release-age=0` to `npm ci`. The release lockfile pins every package, so the flag had no effect, and security scanners that block it stopped the update ([#11262](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11262))
- `/model` and `/scoped-models` now show a model's name next to its ID when the name adds words the ID lacks, such as a renamed `models.json` override ([#5916](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5916), [#11347](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11347))

### Fixed

- MCP sign-in now rejects authorization endpoints and other OAuth metadata URLs that are not `http:` or `https:`. Before, a malicious MCP server could supply a `file:` or custom protocol URL, which pi passed to the platform URL handler.
- Automatic `fd` and `rg` downloads no longer fetch x86-64 binaries on ARM32 and other architectures without a prebuilt release. pi now warns and recommends installing the tool with the system package manager ([#11209](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11209))
- Fixed `/model` search ranking letters scattered over an earlier part of an entry above a real match, for example `opus` listing `gpt-oss-120b` and `claude-sonnet-4.5` before `claude-opus-4.1` ([#11220](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11220), [#11296](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11296))
- Fixed `/resume` search matching scattered letters anywhere in session messages and IDs, for example `1024` matching inside a session UUID. Session names and working directories still match fuzzily; IDs and message text now match only as exact substrings ([#11220](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11220), [#11024](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11024), [#11296](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11296))
- Fixed HTML export showing a blank page for sessions with thousands of entries ([#11225](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11225), [#11293](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11293))
- Fixed HTML export not showing system messages: the system prompt and tools, and later section updates such as after `/reload`. `pi --export` now includes the system prompt and tools too ([#11261](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11261), [#3464](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3464), [#11290](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11290))
- Fixed aborting a bash command on macOS sometimes running the next command of a list such as `long_step; next_step`. pi now stops the process group before killing it ([#11252](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11252), [#11289](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11289))

en.heading: ## [Unreleased]
en.body:
### Added

- Added optional `openBrowserOnConfirm` and `copyCodeOnConfirm` to `device_code` auth events and `OAuthDeviceCodeInfo`. Both default to `true`; set them to `false` to stop clients from offering to open the verification page or copy the code ([#9282](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9282), [#9301](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9301))

### Fixed

- Fixed Claude models that accept mid-conversation system messages rejecting a session with a 400 (`role 'system' must precede an 'assistant' message`) when a system update was followed by an assistant reply with nothing to send to Anthropic, such as an empty reply or another model's reasoning-only reply ([#11091](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11091))
- Fixed Claude models with mid-conversation effort failing with `Invalid effort level` on accounts whose organization caps effort below `high`, even at `low` or `medium` thinking, by sending a fixed `low` top-level effort ([#10063](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10063))

en.heading: ## [Unreleased]
en.body:
### Breaking Changes

- `traceIn(options, fn, context)` takes the context last (was `traceIn(context, options, fn)`), like the rest of the API.

### Added

- `NativeWatchable<T>`: an in-process value that changes and can be watched (`value`, `watch(context)` returning a `NativeWatchHandle<T>`), the in-process counterpart of `Watchable<T>`.
- `WatchHandle<T>` and `WatchEnd`, the one watch API, moved from Durable: a serialized exact-frame observation with `value`, `start(listener)`, `stop()`, and `closed`. `WatchEnd` reasons are `stopped`, `cancelled`, `retired`, `ended`, `listener_error`, and `failed`.
- `Watch<T>`, the one watch handle implementation, moved from Durable: a source creates one per watch and feeds it with `advance(value, ops, context)`, `retire(context)` (last frame `[["r", null]]`, then `retired`), `end()` or `end({ error })`, and `observeCancellation(signal)`. More than 100 undelivered frames collapse to one root replacement `[["r", newest]]`; termination drops the listener and every reference into the source.
- `Watchable<T>`: a value that changes and can be watched (`value`, `watch(context)` returning a `WatchHandle<T>`), the common interface of documents, derives and other observable values.
- `NativeWatchHandle<T>` and its implementation `NativeWatch<T>`: the same lifecycle for in-process values, with listener `(value, context)` and no ops; an overflow collapses to the newest value.

en.heading: ## [Unreleased]
en.body:
### Breaking Changes

- `Storage.commit(writes, adopt, context)` takes an `adopt(seq)` callback, the Session's in-memory adoption of the batch: a storage calls it exactly once, synchronously, once the batch is durable and before its next commit starts, then resolves with `seq`, and never for a commit that fails before the batch is durable. Memory, SQLite, JSONL, and IndexedDB storages do; custom storages and wrappers must call or forward it, and the storage conformance suite checks it. A commit that rejects after its adoption fails the Session without rolling the adopted changes back.
- `Storage.mintId()`'s contract is narrowed to IDs greater than every ID minted since the storage was opened and every ID stored, also across reopen. The bundled storages already behave so.
- Watches use Chord's `WatchHandle` and `WatchEnd` (Durable re-exports both). End reasons are `stopped`, `cancelled`, `retired`, `ended` (was `session_closed`), `listener_error`, and `failed` (was `session_failed`). Retirement is an explicit event of the watched document incarnation (last frame `[["r", null]]`, then `retired`), never inferred from a `null` value. An ended watch drops its listener and every reference into its Session, so a stopped watch that is still referenced keeps only its last value.
- Removed the Chord state getters `Session.documentState()`, `Conversation.viewState()`, and `Harness.taskGraph()`, and the `DocumentState` type; use `watchDoc()`, `Conversation.watch()`, and `Harness.watchTaskGraph()`. Durable no longer uses Chord's `replicatedState()`.

### Added

- `HarnessOptions.readOnly` opens a Harness as a viewer of a session another process drives: open leaves running tasks as committed instead of recovering them, every commit with writes rejects with `ReadOnlySession` before it reaches Storage, and `resume()` and every call that would run tasks reject with it.

### Changed

- Document, conversation view, task graph, and event watches use Chord's `Watch` implementation; behaviour is unchanged.

notes.title: 提交采用、统一 Watch 与只读 Harness
notes.intro: 当前包版本为 1.4.0；此栏列出该版本之后、当前 HEAD 已包含的源码变更。发布状态不能由包版本或本地标签推断。
notes.audience: Durable 存储适配器、观察界面与 CLI 集成维护者。

points.title: 持久化与内存采用有了明确顺序
points.before: 旧 Storage.commit 不接收采用回调。
points.after: 存储持久化后、下次提交开始前同步调用 adopt(seq) 一次，再完成 Promise。
points.why: 让持久提交顺序和内存状态采用顺序一致；采用后失败不能回滚已经采用的状态。
points.action: 自定义存储和 wrapper 转发 adopt，运行存储一致性用例并检查失败窗口。

points.title: 统一使用 Watch 观察当前状态
points.before: documentState、viewState 和 taskGraph getter 暴露 Chord 状态。
points.after: 改用 watchDoc、Conversation.watch 和 watchTaskGraph；统一 WatchHandle 与 WatchEnd。
points.why: 退休由显式事件确认，null 值不代表退休；结束的观察释放 Session 引用。
points.action: 迁移 getter 调用及 session_closed/session_failed 结束原因，验证停止、退休、失败与慢监听恢复。

points.title: 只查看其他进程驱动的会话
points.before: 打开 Harness 会按正常运行方式恢复任务。
points.after: readOnly 打开为查看器，保留已提交运行状态，拒绝写入和任务执行。
points.why: 检查持久状态时避免意外开始运行。
points.action: 分别测试读取、写入、resume 和其他执行入口，确认 ReadOnlySession。

points.title: MCP 授权地址限制协议
points.before: 授权元数据可能把 file 或自定义协议地址交给系统处理。
points.after: 拒绝非 HTTP/HTTPS 的授权端点和相关 OAuth 元数据 URL。
points.why: 外部服务器元数据不能直接决定任意系统 URL 操作。
points.action: 验证正常 HTTPS 登录与非法协议拒绝路径。

packages.description: 产品层：CLI、交互模式、扩展、模型运行时、会话与工具。学习主入口。

en.body:
### New Features

- **Image input for classifiers**: codemode `models.classify()` accepts `images` for TypeSafe's Jev and Cloudflare's Clef models on `typesafe`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, and OpenRouter. See [Use classifier models](docs/models.md#use-classifier-models) and [Codemode](docs/codemode.md#models).
- **Models Configuration reference**: every provider, model, model override, and compatibility field of `models.json`, generated from its schema. See [Models Configuration](docs/models-configuration.md).
- **Summaries without a fixed output cap**: compaction and branch summaries use the model's output limit, so long reasoning no longer makes them fail. See [Compaction](docs/compaction.md#compaction).
- **Codemode waits for a free worker**: parallel scripts and in-process subagents queue instead of failing, and `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` raises the limit. See [Codemode limits](docs/codemode.md#limits).
- **Rex terminal support**: OSC 8 hyperlinks, truecolor, and inline images.

### Added

- Added a Models Configuration reference generated from the `models.json` schema, listing all provider, model, model override, and compatibility fields ([#10790](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10790))
- Codemode `models.classify()` now accepts `images` for TypeSafe's Jev and Cloudflare's Clef models on `typesafe`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, and OpenRouter, and lists Clef Omni and Jev 1.14 on Workers AI.
- Provider-level `compat` in `models.json` now also applies to classifier models, with the System One fields `imageInput` and `sendImageOptInHeader` for proxies that serve another service's classifiers. Extension classifier models accept `compat` too.
- Added `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` to the `minimax` and `minimax-cn` providers, with thinking levels low through max ([#11121](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11121))
- Added support for the Rex terminal: OSC 8 hyperlinks, truecolor, and inline images ([#11131](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11131), [#11150](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11150) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll), [#11183](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11183) by [@nihaals](https://github.com/nihaals))

### Changed

- Provider attribution headers now come from pi-ai's client identity. Extensions' `before_provider_headers` handlers no longer see the OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, and OpenCode attribution headers; returning `null` for one still removes it. Cloudflare requests send pi's detailed `User-Agent` instead of `pi-coding-agent`, as do GitHub release checks for tool downloads, and OpenCode requests send `x-opencode-client` whenever attribution is enabled, not only with a session.
- `generateSummary()` and `generateSummaryWithUsage()` now ignore their `reserveTokens` parameter. Summary requests use the model's output limit instead.
- Changed the default GitHub Copilot model from `gpt-5.4`, which Copilot retired, to `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Changed the default NVIDIA model to `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b` ([#10910](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10910) by [@cv](https://github.com/cv))
- Changed the default Xiaomi model to `mimo-v2.6-pro` for the `xiaomi` and Xiaomi Token Plan providers, since `mimo-v2.5-pro` left the catalog.
- Grok 4.3 and Grok 4.5 on the `xai` provider now offer the `xhigh` thinking level.
- Sign in with ChatGPT: ChatGPT Business workspace usage-limit errors are not retried and tell the user to ask their workspace admin to increase the limit.

### Fixed

- Fixed compaction and branch summaries failing with "generation hit the token cap" when reasoning used most of the fixed summary output limit. Summaries now use the model's output limit, and `compaction.reserveTokens` only controls when compaction starts ([#9512](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9512), [#9075](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9075)).
- Fixed `models.schema.json` missing descriptions for provider and model fields, so editors showed no hints for them ([#10790](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10790))
- Fixed `pi update` failing with "Managed install marker is missing or invalid" when `managed-install.json` starts with a UTF-8 BOM, which Windows PowerShell 5.1 adds when it rewrites the file.
- Fixed HTML export showing literal asterisks for Markdown bold and italic next to CJK punctuation ([#3353](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3353), [#10154](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10154))
- Fixed the terminal staying in mouse-tracking, focus-reporting, Kitty keyboard, and alternate-screen modes when pi exits without its normal terminal teardown, which flooded the shell prompt with escape sequences ([#11170](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11170))
- Fixed concurrent extension `select`/`confirm`/`input`/`editor` dialogs and inline `custom()` components in interactive mode: a second dialog replaced the first and the first promise never settled; closing the visible dialog now shows the previous one again ([#11166](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11166), [#9909](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9909))
- Fixed pasting in the shell hanging after copying text in pi and suspending it with Ctrl+Z on Linux: the background `wl-copy`/`xclip`/`xsel` process that keeps serving the clipboard was suspended along with pi ([#11179](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11179))
- Fixed codemode scripts failing immediately when both codemode workers are busy, for example with parallel codemode calls or in-process subagents. Scripts now wait up to 60 seconds for a free worker, and `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` raises the limit of two workers ([#11184](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11184))
- Fixed extensions failing to load when importing `@earendil-works/pi-ai/models` (e.g. for `clampThinkingLevel`) by exposing the subpath through the extension loader aliases and virtual modules ([#11156](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11156))
- Fixed `mcp.json` files that start with a UTF-8 BOM failing to parse, which skipped all their MCP servers and made `pi mcp add`/`pi mcp remove` fail ([#11191](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11191))
- Fixed `/compact <instructions>` ignoring the instructions when summarizing the start of a turn that compaction splits. When the split turn was the only new content since the last compaction, the instructions were ignored entirely ([#11058](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11058))
- Fixed resumed sessions and `/tree` navigation leaving extension tools inactive when the branch recorded its tools before they were registered, such as tools from extensions installed after the session started. Extension tools the branch never added or removed are now active unless they are registered with `defaultActive: false` ([#11062](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11062), [#11075](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11075))
- Fixed sessions breaking after recovery from a response cut off at the output limit: the truncated tool call was omitted but its tool results were kept, so providers rejected every later request ([#11227](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11227), [#11233](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11233) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed the `grep` tool following `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`, where options such as `--fixed-strings` silently changed regex searches into literal ones. The tool now runs `rg --no-config` ([#11203](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11203), [#11230](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11230) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))

- Fixed the `openai-codex` provider offering `gpt-5.5` and `gpt-5.3-codex-spark`, which always fail for ChatGPT accounts ([#11173](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11173) by [@lucasmeijer](https://github.com/lucasmeijer))

sections.title: New Features
sections.body:
- **Image input for classifiers**: codemode `models.classify()` accepts `images` for TypeSafe's Jev and Cloudflare's Clef models on `typesafe`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, and OpenRouter. See [Use classifier models](docs/models.md#use-classifier-models) and [Codemode](docs/codemode.md#models).

en.body:
### Breaking Changes

- Renamed provider request option `telemetryContext` to `telemetry?: TelemetrySpan`, without a compatibility alias. Pass a parent span, not an adapter.
- The default `User-Agent` is now `pi/<version> (<platform>; <runtime>; <arch>)` instead of `pi (<platform> <release>; <arch>)`, and `@earendil-works/pi-ai/utils/pi-user-agent` (`getPiUserAgent()`) is removed; use `formatUserAgent()`.
- `resolveTranscriptTools()` now takes a `TranscriptToolSupport` (`"none"`, `"additions"`, or `"changes"`) instead of a boolean, and `TranscriptTools.anchorsAdditions` is replaced by `foldedSystemMessages`, the number of leading system messages folded into `requestTools` ([#10940](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10940))

### Added

- Added client identity configuration: an `identity` request option and `createModels({ identity })` default choose the `User-Agent` (`"detailed"` with a version, `"short"`, or custom) and provider attribution headers for OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, and OpenCode from `attribution: { name, url, categories? }`. `withClientIdentity()` applies an identity to a `Models` or `MutableModels` a library receives from its host. `formatUserAgent()`, `getIdentityHeaders()`, `getOpenCodeSessionHeaders()`, `mergeClientIdentity()`, `PI_ATTRIBUTION`, and `PI_AI_VERSION` are exported.
- Bedrock, OpenRouter image generation, pi-messages, and classifier requests now send pi's `User-Agent` too.
- `Models` requests with a `sessionId` to custom providers pointing at OpenCode (`opencode.ai`) now send the `x-opencode-session` header too, like the built-in OpenCode providers.
- Added `AI_TELEMETRY_SCHEMA` and opt-in `pi.ai.request`/`pi.ai.poll` tracing around Models requests, with content-free first-event, block-size, and final usage attributes, plus duration, token, and USD cost metrics through `telemetry.metrics`.
- Failed model request spans report `provider_error` status with up to 500 error-message characters; cancelled requests keep `ok` status with `stop: "aborted"`.
- Added `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` to the `minimax` and `minimax-cn` providers, with thinking levels low through max sent as `output_config.effort`. Thinking cannot be turned off for this model. New MiniMax models from models.dev now appear without a manual allowlist entry; only the older M2, M2.1, M2.5, and M2.5-highspeed models stay hidden ([#11121](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11121))
- Sign in with ChatGPT: ChatGPT Business workspace usage-limit errors are not retried and tell the user to ask their workspace admin to increase the limit.
- Added image input to System One classifiers: `ClassifierContext.images` now works with Jev on `typesafe` (experimental there, opted in with the `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images` header) and `cloudflare-workers-ai`, with Clef on `cloudflare-workers-ai`, and with OpenRouter decision models whose catalog lists image input. Each service gets its own wire form: TypeSafe `assets`, Clef `images` data URLs, or OpenRouter `image_url` parts in the state.
- Added `compat` to System One classifier models (`SystemOneCompat`, with `imageInput` and `sendImageOptInHeader`). Built-in catalog entries set it explicitly; models without it detect the form from the provider, `baseUrl`, and model ID.
- Added the `@cf/cloudflare/clef-omni` and `typesafe/jev-1.14.0` classifier models to `cloudflare-workers-ai`.

### Changed

- Grok 4.3 and Grok 4.5 on the `xai` provider now offer the `xhigh` thinking level, matching the reasoning efforts xAI supports for these models.

### Fixed

- Fixed Cloudflare Workers AI classifier catalog data: Clef Flash now costs $0.038 per million input tokens with a 24,576-token context window, and Jev costs $0.042 per million input tokens instead of being listed as free.
- Fixed whitespace-only tool output (for example a bare `\r\n` from bash) being sent as-is to OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Google providers; it now uses the same placeholder as empty output, since some providers reject whitespace-only tool content with a 400 ([#8720](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8720))
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering for gateway upstream failures such as `upstream_error: Upstream request failed`, `upstream_stream_read_error`, and `Upstream HTTP/2 stream failed` ([#10920](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10920))
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering when the Google Vertex OAuth token refresh fails with a transient network error such as `request to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token failed, reason:` ([#10996](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10996))
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering for `stream disconnected before completion` errors relayed by proxies that wrap the Codex CLI ([#11057](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11057))
- Fixed automatic retry treating digits inside request ids or other numbers (for example `req_011CU503xyz` or `5242880 bytes`) as retryable HTTP status codes ([#11057](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11057))
- Fixed OpenAI Responses deferred tool loads rewriting the top-level tool list, and losing the prompt cache, on every load after a tool removal. Models with `additional_tools` now declare all tools in `additional_tools` items, starting with one at the head of the input, so removals (announced as text) and redefinitions no longer rewrite the prefix. Tool search and Kimi tool messages rewrite the top-level tools once per removal or redeclaration and keep later loads anchored ([#10940](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10940))
- Fixed GitHub Copilot requests whose body exceeds Copilot's size limit (HTTP 413 `failed to parse request`, for example sessions with many large images) failing instead of being detected as context overflow. Any HTTP 413 now counts as context overflow, so callers can compact and retry ([#11016](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11016) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed the `openai-codex` provider listing `gpt-5.5` and `gpt-5.3-codex-spark`, which the Codex backend rejects for ChatGPT accounts. Both models are removed ([#11173](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11173) by [@lucasmeijer](https://github.com/lucasmeijer))

en.body:
### Breaking Changes

- Custom `Context` implementations must provide `telemetry: TelemetrySpan`; use the no-op span `NOOP_TELEMETRY_CONTEXT` when disabled. `withTelemetry()` accepts spans, not adapters.

### Added

- `@earendil-works/chord/telemetry-sqlite`: portable SQLite telemetry recording with bounded settled-span queues, ten-second metric aggregates, periodic flushes, and retention cleanup.
- `Context.telemetry` is an explicit, non-optional telemetry parent (no-op by default). `withTelemetry(telemetry, context)` derives it without changing values or cancellation; `traceIn(context, options, fn)` starts a child span and passes its derived context to the callback.
- `@earendil-works/chord/sqlite`: portable SQLite interfaces, atomic migration runner, and schema-prefix validation, with Node (`/sqlite/node`) and Cloudflare Durable Object (`/sqlite/cloudflare`) drivers. Moved from Durable, which keeps its storage implementations and re-exports the moved public names.
- `@earendil-works/chord/output`: `Progress` takes an optional `ProgressClock` (`now`, `setTimer`) to pace commits on, by default `Date.now` and `setTimeout`.

sections.title: Added
sections.body:
- `@earendil-works/chord/telemetry-sqlite`: portable SQLite telemetry recording with bounded settled-span queues, ten-second metric aggregates, periodic flushes, and retention cleanup.

Moved from Durable, which keeps its storage implementations and re-exports the moved public names.

实验性持久 Agent Harness：逐会话配置、生成/工具任务、队列、子会话、Watch 与内存/JSONL/SQLite 存储。

en.body:
### Breaking Changes

- `TaskRuntime.sleep()` is removed: it waited inside a phase, which holds an invocation and, after a restart, reruns the phase and restarts the wait. A task now ends its phase asleep with `runtime.sleepUntil(until, checkpoint, context)` or by returning `{ status: "sleeping", until, checkpoint }` from `runtime.commit()`; move the work after the wait into the next phase and carry what it needs in the checkpoint. `TaskRuntime.setTimer()` paces work inside a phase without waiting for it.
- Tasks have a `sleeping` status, so code that handles every `TaskState`, `TaskGraphState`, or `TaskInspection` state needs a case for it.
- Opening a SQLite storage migrates it to schema version 2 automatically, rebuilding its task table. A migrated database cannot be opened by 1.3.0 or earlier, so a deployment cannot roll back past this release. JSONL storage needs no migration, but 1.3.0 or earlier never resumes a sleeping task it finds (a run's conversation stays busy).
- `TaskRuntime` has `sleepUntil()` and `setTimer()`, and `ToolExecutionApi` has `now()`: code that builds either object by hand, such as a test fake or a tool wrapper that does not spread the original, must add them.
- A task cut off by a crash 5 times in a row without committing a new state is parked instead of run again (see the crash-loop guard under Added); set `settings.restartLimit` to `Infinity` to keep the old behavior. `TaskInspection`'s blocked reasons include `restart_limit`.
- `defineDoc()` and `defineDocFamily()` require an explicit `checkpointWhen` predicate on every definition; there is no default. Use `() => false` to keep ordinary changes as deltas, or supply a policy that periodically writes a base.

### Added

- Added `IndexedDbStorage` (`@earendil-works/pi-durable/storage/indexeddb`), a browser storage backed by IndexedDB.
- `HarnessOptions.telemetry` emits the content-free `DURABLE_TELEMETRY_SCHEMA`: public submission admission spans, task phase spans (including extension tasks), committed entry and submission events, running phase-change checkpoints, and nested-tool replay events. Optional propagation stores opaque carriers on submissions and tasks so queued inputs and reopened tasks retain their trace; `TaskOptions.trace` accepts a carrier override or `"root"` (absence inherits the creator's carrier); creation-time `links` connect inputs sharing a run, while steer admissions link to the running trace. Internal admissions emit events without a submit span. Optional metrics record phase duration and live task counts. Failed phases record fixed error-status categories (`task_faulted`, `task_failed`, `task_orphaned`) and diagnostics capped at 500 characters; aborted phases keep status `ok`. Every `onReport` report also emits a fixed-field `pi.durable.report` event on its current span (dropped by the NOOP span when there is none), plus a `pi.durable.reports` counter by type; report telemetry contains no error payload and leaves the callback unchanged. Clock failures report without a phase context. Generation and compaction forward their phase context to pi-ai requests.
- `settings.compaction.modelOverrides` sets compaction thresholds per model, keyed by exact `"provider/modelId"`, so one harness can serve small- and large-window models; the threshold check, overflow recovery, and the compaction task use the entry of the model they act for ([#10942](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10942)).
- Durable sleeps: a sleeping task holds no invocation, survives restarts, and resumes at its checkpoint once the Harness clock reaches `until`.
- `HarnessOptions.setTimer` arms the timers of the Session, the scheduler, and its tasks (progress throttles, idle-memory eviction, sleeps), also for `createSession()`; with `now`, they run on a host or fake clock. A foreground timer the host throws on or declines falls back to `setTimeout`. `ToolExecutionApi.now()` reads the Harness clock.
- `Harness.wake()` and `HarnessOptions.onWake` tell a host when the Session next needs a process: `active` while work can run, `at` for the earliest sleep. With `onWake`, the Harness keeps no timer for sleeps, so a Cloudflare Durable Object can hibernate and wake on its alarm, calling `resume()`.
- Crash-loop guard: open counts the restarts of each task that a crash, eviction, or reset cut off (`TaskRecord.restarts`); a close writes the tasks it stopped back as `pending` uncounted, and a new state the task commits starts the count over. At `settings.restartLimit` the task is parked: blocked with reason `restart_limit` in `inspect()` and the task graph, not active in `wake()`, and reported once. `Harness.retryTask(id)` runs it again. An abort handler cut off that many times ends its task `faulted`.
- `onReport(error, info)`: `info` (`ReportInfo`) says what happened in `type`: `session_failed`; `task_faulted`, `task_parked`, `migration_failed`, `task_outdated`, or `task_error` with the task and the extension that installed it; `extension_error` with the extension's name; `host_error` with the failing `HostCallback`; or `listener_error`.
- `settings.afterFailedRun`: a run that fails with `model_error` or `no_model` keeps the inputs queued behind it (`keep`, the default), starts the next run with them (`continue`), or settles them `unanswered` with reason `run_failed` (`withdraw`).
- The task graph shows why a task cannot run (`TaskGraphNode.blocked`: `missing_task`, `task_too_old`, `migration_failed`, or `restart_limit`) and follows registry changes and failed migrations.
- Added `HarnessOptions.identity` (a pi-ai `ClientIdentity`) to set the `User-Agent` and provider attribution of every model request through the Harness, including hooks and tools. `api.models` in tools and hooks is now a wrapper of the host's `Models` that adds the identity, not the same object.
- `HarnessOptions.models` and `HarnessOptions.settings` also accept a function returning the current value, like `env`. Generation, compaction, hooks and tools call it at each use (`api.models` reads the current value at each access), so a host can replace its model configuration or settings without reopening the Harness. A plain object still works.

### Changed

- A task phase that faults is reported through `onReport` (as `task_faulted`), not only recorded in its outcome.
- `onReport` gets a second argument, `info`, and `TaskRuntime.report()` takes an optional `from` (see Added); an `onReport` written for one argument still works.
- Generation retry backoffs, deferred-response polls, and compaction retry backoffs sleep instead of waiting in a running phase, so a process can stop or hibernate during them. A record an earlier version stored mid-backoff sleeps again when it resumes before its time. A deferred poll whose model is gone after a reopen now fails `no_model` once the poll is due, not at once.
- Code mode measures script deadlines and wall time on the Harness clock (`HarnessOptions.now`) instead of `Date.now()`.
- SQLite drivers, portable interfaces, and the generic migration runner now come from `@earendil-works/chord/sqlite`. Existing Durable SQLite entry points keep re-exporting their public names; storage helpers and Durable schema migrations stay here.
- `ToolControl.terminate` is now typed `boolean` instead of `true`, matching `pi-agent-core` and `pi-coding-agent`; `false` does not end the run ([#10858](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10858)).

### Fixed

- In Cloudflare Workers with `nodejs_compat`, the timers that evict idle documents and contexts were armed, since timers there have an `unref()`; a pending one kept a Durable Object from hibernating and blocked its eviction. They are now declined in Workers, and memory is freed at later commits.
- The README's Errors section now limits the `StorageRequestError` exemption to reads: a `StorageRequestError` thrown by `commit()` or `mintId()` fails the Harness like any other storage error ([#11014](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11014)).
- The Node environment now detects the legacy WSL `bash.exe` launcher from `%SystemRoot%` instead of assuming `C:\Windows` ([#9501](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9501) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll)).

en.body:
### Breaking Changes

- Adapters trust typed instrumentation inputs; behavior for malformed values is unspecified. Carrier extraction checks required string identities, without validating their format.
- Adapters must implement `TelemetrySpan.addLink()`. Normalized span snapshots include carrier-shaped context and parent identities and ordered links.
- Adapters with optional metric or propagation capabilities must carry them through `TelemetryContext.metrics` and `TelemetryContext.propagation` on roots, spans, and extracted parents.

### Added

- Opaque string-map carriers and optional `TelemetryPropagation` injection/extraction, with passive root fallback for absent or invalid carriers and shared `NOOP_TELEMETRY_PROPAGATION`.
- Initial `SpanOptions.links` and late `span.addLink()` with context targets and optional attributes, including settled target spans and extracted remote parents.
- Optional `TelemetryMetrics` counters, up-down counters, and histograms with boundary hints and exemplar contexts, plus shared `NOOP_TELEMETRY_METRICS` instruments.
- Optional context capability members, populated by the no-op and in-memory adapters and checked by adapter conformance.
- `NOOP_TELEMETRY_CONTEXT` is typed as `TelemetrySpan`, matching the shared inert span it provides.
- Metric schema definitions and `createTypedMetrics()` with exact instrument names, kinds, and required/optional low-cardinality attributes.
- In-memory propagation across processes, link and measurement snapshots, and adapter conformance cases for propagation, links, and optional metrics.
- `StoredSpan`, `StoredTrace`, and `TelemetryStore` define backend-independent trace discovery, trace retrieval, and metric queries. `@earendil-works/pi-telemetry/render` exports `renderTrace()` for plain-text span trees with attributes, durations, errors, events, and cross-trace links; merged spans are deduplicated by ID and links are never followed.

### Added

- Added detection of the Rex terminal (`TERM_PROGRAM=rex`) with OSC 8 hyperlinks, truecolor, and Kitty images. notes.title: 1.3.0 之后：持久睡眠、崩溃保护与显式遥测
notes.intro: 1.4.0 日志于 2026-10-21 归档持久睡眠、崩溃保护、IndexedDB、客户端身份、分类器图像输入与摘要预算等变化。当前 HEAD 还有后续 Unreleased 变更，需继续阅读上一栏。
notes.audience: 持久任务、存储适配器、遥测与模型接入维护者。

points.title: 等待变为可持久睡眠
points.before: 在 phase 内等待占用 invocation，重启可能重新开始等待。
points.after: 用 sleepUntil(until, checkpoint, context) 或 commit 返回 sleeping 结束阶段，到期从 checkpoint 继续；setTimer 只用于阶段内节奏。
points.why: 睡眠任务不持有 invocation，可跨重启；switch TaskState 时必须处理 sleeping。
points.action: 把等待后的工作放入下一阶段，按宿主 clock 验证重启与 wake/onWake。SQLite 自动迁移到 schema v2，不能回退到 1.3.0 或更早版本读取。

points.title: 连续崩溃的任务会停放
points.before: 异常重启可能持续重新执行同一任务。
points.after: 连续 5 次未提交新状态的崩溃会触发 restart_limit，inspect 与任务图呈现阻塞，retryTask 可显式重试。
points.why: 区分运行中断和业务新状态，避免无限崩溃循环。
points.action: 观察 onReport 与 blocked 原因；只有明确需要旧行为时才使用 Infinity。

points.title: SQLite 基础层迁入 Chord
points.before: 通用 SQLite 接口、驱动和迁移器位于 Durable。
points.after: Chord 提供 sqlite、sqlite/node、sqlite/cloudflare；Durable 保留存储实现与公开名称再导出。
points.why: 共享数据库基础层可供宿主使用，不必依赖持久 Agent 的业务存储。
points.action: 区分通用数据库迁移与 Durable 自身 schema 迁移，核验前缀与元数据表名限制。

points.title: 请求遥测传入 span 而非 adapter
points.before: 旧选项名为 telemetryContext。
points.after: 改为 telemetry?: TelemetrySpan，无兼容别名；Models 可记录 request/poll、用量和固定错误状态。
points.why: 显式传递父 span 保持调用归属；不能把全局适配器当作当前操作。
points.action: 同步调用方与测试替身，取消仍保持 ok 且 stop=aborted；检查错误诊断与内容边界。

points.title: 摘要输出上限与压缩触发阈值分离
points.before: 固定摘要输出上限可能被 reasoning 消耗，产生 token cap 错误。
points.after: 摘要使用模型输出上限，reserveTokens 仅控制压缩开始时机；generateSummary 相关参数不再约束输出。
points.why: 压缩触发容量和摘要生成预算是两个维度。
points.action: 分别验证触发阈值与高推理摘要，不用调 reserveTokens 来声称提高摘要输出限制。

packages.description: 产品层：CLI、交互模式、扩展、模型运行时、会话与工具。学习主入口。

en.body:
### New Features

- **Choose where `/share` uploads**: `sessionShareDestination` selects `auto`, `gist`, or `radius`. See [Sessions and context](docs/settings.md#sessions-and-context) and [Export or share a session](docs/sessions.md#export-or-share-a-session).
- **Cache-preserving thinking level changes on OpenAI GPT-6**: changing the thinking level mid-session with an API key keeps the prompt cache.
- **Kimi Code over Chat Completions**: tools added mid-conversation no longer invalidate the prompt cache. `models.json` base URL overrides must now include `/v1`. See [Providers](docs/providers.md).
- **Clean model switching**: thinking from a previous model is dropped instead of being shown to the new model as text.
- **Resumed sessions keep their active tools**: `--tools +name`/`-name` applies on top of them. See [Tools](docs/settings.md#tools).

### Added

- Changing the thinking level mid-session on OpenAI GPT-6 models (API key) now keeps the prompt cache ([#10853](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10853))
- Added the `sessionShareDestination` setting to choose automatic, GitHub gist, or Radius uploads for `/share` ([#10870](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10870) by [@vegarsti](https://github.com/vegarsti))

### Changed

- Changed the `kimi-coding` provider to use OpenAI Chat Completions at `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, the protocol used by the official Kimi Code client. K3, K3-256K, and Kimi For Coding now accept tools added mid-conversation without invalidating the prompt cache. `models.json` overrides of the `kimi-coding` base URL must now include `/v1` ([#10720](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10720))
- Changed model switching to drop thinking blocks from earlier assistant messages produced by a different model, instead of sending them as plain text. The new model previously saw the old model's reasoning as part of its replies and could start writing its own reasoning into the visible answer ([#10995](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10995))

### Fixed

- Pinned internal Pi dependencies to exact release versions to prevent fresh installs from mixing incompatible packages ([#10865](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10865))
- Fixed resumed sessions dropping tools activated during the session. Resume now restores the session's active tools, with `--tools +name`/`-name` entries applied to them, unless `--tools` with tool names, `--no-tools`, or `--no-builtin-tools` selects tools explicitly ([#10785](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10785))
- Fixed stopping a codemode script or reaching its deadline waiting for a non-interruptible built-in to return on Bun ([#10748](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10748))
- Fixed repeated codemode timeouts or aborts accumulating surviving workers; admission now limits live workers to two across sessions, counting cancelled workers until actual exit ([#10748](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10748))
- Fixed `--model` choosing a provider by catalog order when several providers offer the match; Pi now prefers the provider with credentials and otherwise reports the ambiguity. `--models` and `enabledModels` add a model for each provider that offers it and warn about the ambiguity ([#10160](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10160))
- Fixed `read` line-range labels for numeric-string or null arguments in the TUI, session tree, HTML exports, and examples ([#9887](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9887))
- Fixed the Nix flake build failing when a provider switched APIs: the model catalog pin is now refreshed from the newest published catalog when its model API groups differ, and releases pin the newest catalog and build with it before tagging ([#10985](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10985))
- Fixed the Nix package putting its Node.js first on `PATH`, which made bash tool shells use Pi's Node instead of the user's `node`/`npm`. Pi's Node is now only a fallback ([#10519](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10519))
- Fixed prompt templates dropping empty quoted arguments (`""` or `''`), which shifted later positional arguments and prevented positional defaults from applying ([#10867](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10867))
- Fixed the Nix package build failing in its install check because it still expected chord and esbuild, which Pi no longer depends on
- Fixed tool-call argument parsing dropping fields when a string contains an invalid `\u` escape such as `\usepackage` ([#10868](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10868))
- Fixed Anthropic and Bedrock Claude requests failing with a 400 when an error tool result contains images; the images are now sent after the tool results of the turn, so the model still sees them ([#10794](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10794))
- Fixed OpenCode Go Gemini models failing with a 404 by moving OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go to the `opencode.ai/inference` endpoints, and added Google Generative AI support to the OpenCode Go provider
- Fixed OpenCode Go MiniMax M2.7 failing with "Model does not support this protocol" by using the Anthropic Messages API
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering for gateway `Unable to forward upstream stream` errors ([#10920](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10920))
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering for `The service is temporarily unavailable` errors, which also made compaction fail on the first attempt ([#10965](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10965))
- Fixed OpenAI-compatible responses showing thinking after the answer when a proxy such as LiteLLM sends reasoning and content in the same stream chunk ([#10926](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10926))
- Fixed Gemini 4 Argon requests on Google Vertex failing with "Thinking budget is not supported", and its thinking level being ignored on the Gemini API ([#10890](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10890))
- Fixed Xiaomi MiMo models failing with a 400 at the `minimal` thinking level; they now expose only the `off` and `high` levels ([#10818](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10818))
- Fixed `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol` using a 272K context window instead of the 500K window Codex now provides ([#10840](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10840))
- Fixed tool calls whose final arguments are malformed JSON silently running with only the fields parsed before the error; they now fail validation and show the model the raw arguments it sent ([#10897](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10897))
- Fixed Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Opus 5 not supporting the `off` thinking level ([#10753](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10753))
- Fixed `done()` of an extension's `ctx.ui.custom({ overlay: true })` closing the topmost overlay instead of its own, which left the finished overlay on screen and another extension's dialog unresolved ([#10648](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10648), [#10999](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10999) by [@masonc15](https://github.com/masonc15))

The new model previously saw the old model's reasoning as part of its replies and could start writing its own reasoning into the visible answer ([#10995](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10995))

- Fixed tool-call argument parsing dropping fields when a string contains an invalid `\u` escape such as `\usepackage` ([#10868](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10868))
- Fixed Anthropic and Bedrock Claude requests failing with a 400 when an error tool result contains images; the images are now sent after the tool results of the turn, so the model still sees them ([#10794](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10794))
- Fixed OpenCode Go Gemini models failing with a 404 by moving OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go to the `opencode.ai/inference` endpoints, and added Google Generative AI support to the OpenCode Go provider
- Fixed OpenCode Go MiniMax M2.7 failing with "Model does not support this protocol" by using the Anthropic Messages API
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering for gateway `Unable to forward upstream stream` errors ([#10920](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10920))

- Fixed Gemini 4 Argon requests on Google Vertex failing with "Thinking budget is not supported", and its thinking level being ignored on the Gemini API, by sending `thinkingLevel` for Gemini 4 and later models ([#10890](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10890))
- Fixed Xiaomi MiMo models failing with a 400 at the `minimal` thinking level by sending only the documented thinking on/off toggle and exposing only the `off` and `high` levels ([#10818](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10818))

packages.description: 独立对象运行时：契约、句柄、状态、principal 变体、跨进程连接与热重载。

en.body:
### Breaking Changes - Terminology follows the concepts: a reference (what `get` returns) is `Ref` (was `Handle`), its status `RefStatus` (was `HandleStatus`); what a factory returns is `ImplementationOf` (was `BehaviorOf`); a resource's options are a `ResourceDeclaration` (was `ResourceSpec`); epochs are code versions: `Ctx.codeVersion`, `RootOptions.codeVersion`, `Host.codeVersion`/`previousCodeVersion`, and the `codeVersion` fields of frames and reload reports (all were `epoch`). Docs and messages say object (was record) and reference (was handle and hold); the `hold` and `release` frame types keep their names - A remote object's variant is named `variant` (was `kind`): factories return `{ variant: "editor", … }`, references expose `ref.variant` and `shape.variant`, and the `shape` frame carries `variant`. `variant` is reserved as a member name; `kind` no longer is - Links have a protocol version (`PROTOCOL_VERSION`, now 2), announced in `hello`. Peers of different versions do not talk: the side that notices closes the link with reason `protocol-version `, and both sides report it through `LinkOptions.onProtocolMismatch`. Peers without a version (older Chord) are refused - `serve(…, { lifetime })` replaces `eager`: `"referenced"` (the default) creates an object at the first `get` of its address and disposes it after the last reference is released (plus `linger`); `"host"` creates the type's one object when its facet loads and keeps it until the host closes or a reload removes its facet. `lifetime: "host"` is refused at `serve` for remote types, for inputs that do not accept `{}` and together with `linger`; every `get` of such a type reaches its one object, created for the host principal, and another input is `invalid/input`. `eager: { input }` and the extra objects host-principal `get`s with other inputs created are gone. Only `"host"` objects may register (reason `invalid/not_host_lifetime`, was `not_eager`). `LoadOptions.awaitHostObjects` replaces `awaitEager` - Declarations are calls by name: `self.state(name, schema, initial, { version?, migrate? })` returns the cell, `self.resource(name, { version, deps?, exclusive?, open, close? })` the resource (`rev` is now `version`), `self.on(name, source, [select,] handler)` declares a listener; `self.derive(sources, fn)` and `self.task(fn)` take no name. `cell()`, `derivation()`, `resource()`, `listener()`, `self.resources`, `self.listen`, `self.tasks` and the declaration maps are gone, and so are the types `CellDecl`, `ResourceDecl`, `DerivationDecl`, `ListenerDecl`. A repeated name of one kind in a run is `invalid/duplicate` - State versions belong to cells: `ServeOptions.state` is gone; a cell's `version` (default 1) and `migrate(old, from)` replace it. A raised version migrates only that cell; a lowered one refuses the reload - A derivation is new at every reload (computed at the commit) instead of kept with its function replaced. A listener whose state source a reload replaced subscribes again and gets the current value again: listeners on state must reconcile. Listeners on state subscribe when they activate, so they get the value current then - `method(args?, result?)`: without arguments a method is called `ref.name(ctx?)` and implemented `(ctx) => …`; without a result it is void (callers get `undefined`). Descriptions record both by leaving `args`/`result` out (fingerprints of such methods change), `call` frames omit `args` and `result` frames `value` for them. Coverage requires both sides to agree on arguments; a void consumer accepts a result - Remote contracts declare where their objects live, and callers no longer name a host: `remote(name, { …, host: hostNamed("server") })` or `host: hostFamily("session:", "session")` (the host `session:` + the input's required string field `session`, checked by TypeScript). `host` is required on remote contracts; `GetOptions.at` is removed. A `get` normalizes the input, resolves the host, and acquires locally or over the link to it. `serve` refuses a type whose placement does not include the host (also at a reload), a host refuses a hold whose input its own contract places elsewhere (`invalid/placement`), and a relay refuses a hold whose target disagrees with its contract token. The placement is part of the description and fingerprint; coverage requires equal placements, and `accepts` adapters do not bridge placements. Remote references are addressed by type, normalized input and principal, without a host name. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is 3 (remote tokens carry `host`; a hold's input is normalized). New exports: `hostNamed`, `hostFamily`, `Placement`, `PlacementFor`, `HostNamed`, `HostFamily` - `FacetApi` has a `signal` (below): code that builds a `FacetApi` by hand, for example to wrap `serve`, must pass it on - Principals are typed and supplied by the app: `createHost

`, `Host

`, `defineFacet

`, `FacetApi

`, `Serve

`, `Factory`, `Self

`, `Ctx

`, `GetOptions

`, `RootOptions

`, `Route

`, `AcceptOptions

` and `PrincipalMatch

` take the app's principal type (default `unknown`), so factories, methods, listeners and tasks narrow on it without casts. Chord invents no principals any more: `createHost({ self })` (required) is the principal of the host's own code, replacing the built-in `hostPrincipal` (`{ host: true }`, removed); `connect(link, { principal })` (required) is what the parent's own requests act as, replacing `{ host: }`; `Route.principal` is required, replacing the default `{ host: }`. `HostOptions.upstream` is `{ link, principal, ...LinkOptions }` (was a link, with `upstreamOptions`). The host's own principal is recognized by `principalKey`, not object identity. The `Principal` type is gone; `ConnectOptions` and `PrincipalPattern` are new - `serve(type, factory, { lifetime: "host" })` compiles only for a local type whose input has no required fields, and without `linger`; `serve` still refuses the rest at runtime. `ServeOptions` is a union of `ReferencedServeOptions` and `HostServeOptions`, and `serve` takes `ServeOptionsFor` - An awaited reference has its state, local or remote. `ctx.get` and `host.get` are async: they resolve once the reference is live and every state member of its variant has its first snapshot, and reject with the activation error, `aborted` (the ctx aborted or its call settled; `host.get`'s `signal`) or `unavailable/ready_timeout` after `HostOptions.readyTimeout` (default 60000 ms), releasing only that reference. `host.hold` is the synchronous form (possibly `loading`) for UI runtimes; `ref.ready` stays. `self.get` stays synchronous: an object goes live only once its references are ready and hydrated, and the state it exposes or derives from (also forwarded from a remote reference held another way) has its values; activation and reload prepare wait at most `readyTimeout` (a reference cycle across hosts fails with a hint instead of hanging) - State members are typed `T` (was `T | undefined`) and `StateSource` is `Readable`. Reading state before the first hydration throws `not_ready`, outside the current variant `not_in_variant`, after the reference ended its end error. A remote reference is a union discriminated by `variant`: another variant's members are reachable only after narrowing. `MembersOf` is gone. sections.title: Breaking Changes
sections.body:
- Terminology follows the concepts: a reference (what `get` returns) is `Ref` (was `Handle`), its status `RefStatus` (was `HandleStatus`); what a factory returns is `ImplementationOf` (was `BehaviorOf`); a resource's options are a `ResourceDeclaration` (was `ResourceSpec`); epochs are code versions: `Ctx.codeVersion`, `RootOptions.codeVersion`, `Host.codeVersion`/`previousCodeVersion`, and the `codeVersion` fields of frames and reload reports (all were `epoch`). Docs and messages say object (was record) and reference (was handle and hold); the `hold` and `release` frame types keep their names - A remote object's variant is named `variant` (was `kind`): factories return `{ variant: "editor", … }`, references expose `ref.variant` and `shape.variant`, and the `shape` frame carries `variant`. `variant` is reserved as a member name; `kind` no longer is - Links have a protocol version (`PROTOCOL_VERSION`, now 2), announced in `hello`. Peers of different versions do not talk: the side that notices closes the link with reason `protocol-version `, and both sides report it through `LinkOptions.onProtocolMismatch`. Peers without a version (older Chord) are refused - `serve(…, { lifetime })` replaces `eager`: `"referenced"` (the default) creates an object at the first `get` of its address and disposes it after the last reference is released (plus `linger`); `"host"` creates the type's one object when its facet loads and keeps it until the host closes or a reload removes its facet. `lifetime: "host"` is refused at `serve` for remote types, for inputs that do not accept `{}` and together with `linger`; every `get` of such a type reaches its one object, created for the host principal, and another input is `invalid/input`. `eager: { input }` and the extra objects host-principal `get`s with other inputs created are gone. Only `"host"` objects may register (reason `invalid/not_host_lifetime`, was `not_eager`). `LoadOptions.awaitHostObjects` replaces `awaitEager` - Declarations are calls by name: `self.state(name, schema, initial, { version?, migrate? })` returns the cell, `self.resource(name, { version, deps?, exclusive?, open, close? })` the resource (`rev` is now `version`), `self.on(name, source, [select,] handler)` declares a listener; `self.derive(sources, fn)` and `self.task(fn)` take no name. `cell()`, `derivation()`, `resource()`, `listener()`, `self.resources`, `self.listen`, `self.tasks` and the declaration maps are gone, and so are the types `CellDecl`, `ResourceDecl`, `DerivationDecl`, `ListenerDecl`. A repeated name of one kind in a run is `invalid/duplicate` - State versions belong to cells: `ServeOptions.state` is gone; a cell's `version` (default 1) and `migrate(old, from)` replace it. A raised version migrates only that cell; a lowered one refuses the reload - A derivation is new at every reload (computed at the commit) instead of kept with its function replaced. A listener whose state source a reload replaced subscribes again and gets the current value again: listeners on state must reconcile. Listeners on state subscribe when they activate, so they get the value current then - `method(args?, result?)`: without arguments a method is called `ref.name(ctx?)` and implemented `(ctx) => …`; without a result it is void (callers get `undefined`). Descriptions record both by leaving `args`/`result` out (fingerprints of such methods change), `call` frames omit `args` and `result` frames `value` for them. Coverage requires both sides to agree on arguments; a void consumer accepts a result - Remote contracts declare where their objects live, and callers no longer name a host: `remote(name, { …, host: hostNamed("server") })` or `host: hostFamily("session:", "session")` (the host `session:` + the input's required string field `session`, checked by TypeScript). `host` is required on remote contracts; `GetOptions.at` is removed. A `get` normalizes the input, resolves the host, and acquires locally or over the link to it. `serve` refuses a type whose placement does not include the host (also at a reload), a host refuses a hold whose input its own contract places elsewhere (`invalid/placement`), and a relay refuses a hold whose target disagrees with its contract token. The placement is part of the description and fingerprint; coverage requires equal placements, and `accepts` adapters do not bridge placements. Remote references are addressed by type, normalized input and principal, without a host name. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is 3 (remote tokens carry `host`; a hold's input is normalized). New exports: `hostNamed`, `hostFamily`, `Placement`, `PlacementFor`, `HostNamed`, `HostFamily` - `FacetApi` has a `signal` (below): code that builds a `FacetApi` by hand, for example to wrap `serve`, must pass it on - Principals are typed and supplied by the app: `createHost

`, `Host

`, `defineFacet

`, `FacetApi

`, `Serve

`, `Factory`, `Self

`, `Ctx

`, `GetOptions

`, `RootOptions

`, `Route

`, `AcceptOptions

` and `PrincipalMatch

` take the app's principal type (default `unknown`), so factories, methods, listeners and tasks narrow on it without casts. Chord invents no principals any more: `createHost({ self })` (required) is the principal of the host's own code, replacing the built-in `hostPrincipal` (`{ host: true }`, removed); `connect(link, { principal })` (required) is what the parent's own requests act as, replacing `{ host: }`; `Route.principal` is required, replacing the default `{ host: }`. `HostOptions.upstream` is `{ link, principal, ...LinkOptions }` (was a link, with `upstreamOptions`). The host's own principal is recognized by `principalKey`, not object identity. The `Principal` type is gone; `ConnectOptions` and `PrincipalPattern` are new - `serve(type, factory, { lifetime: "host" })` compiles only for a local type whose input has no required fields, and without `linger`; `serve` still refuses the rest at runtime. `ServeOptions` is a union of `ReferencedServeOptions` and `HostServeOptions`, and `serve` takes `ServeOptionsFor` - An awaited reference has its state, local or remote. `ctx.get` and `host.get` are async: they resolve once the reference is live and every state member of its variant has its first snapshot, and reject with the activation error, `aborted` (the ctx aborted or its call settled; `host.get`'s `signal`) or `unavailable/ready_timeout` after `HostOptions.readyTimeout` (default 60000 ms), releasing only that reference. `host.hold` is the synchronous form (possibly `loading`) for UI runtimes; `ref.ready` stays. `self.get` stays synchronous: an object goes live only once its references are ready and hydrated, and the state it exposes or derives from (also forwarded from a remote reference held another way) has its values; activation and reload prepare wait at most `readyTimeout` (a reference cycle across hosts fails with a hint instead of hanging) - State members are typed `T` (was `T | undefined`) and `StateSource` is `Readable`. Reading state before the first hydration throws `not_ready`, outside the current variant `not_in_variant`, after the reference ended its end error. A remote reference is a union discriminated by `variant`: another variant's members are reachable only after narrowing. `MembersOf` is gone. A listener added before a member is readable gets its snapshot then (no `undefined` snapshot first) - A remote reference stays subscribed to its variant's state while held, with or without listeners (it no longer forgets its value when the last listener leaves). `GetOptions.state: false` makes a method-only reference: no state unless another reference to the object wants it, ready once live - `Shape.codeVersion` and the `shape` frame's `codeVersion` are gone - `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is 4: a `hold` implies the state of its variant (`state: false` opts out until `sub`; `unsub` stops it); the provider answers with units, a `shape` listing the members the consumer lacks (`state`) followed by their snapshots; `state` frames are addressed by hold and member (`hold`, `m`) with `as: "snap" | "reset" | "ops" | "error"` and `value` (absent: `undefined`); `sub`/`unsub` take a hold; `resync` asks for a member again; `again` marks a re-hold after a link loss; `origin` (replacing `client`) names the client connection a hold comes from

en.body:
### Breaking Changes

- Worker-backed results and `close()` now settle after requesting shutdown, not after worker exit. Hosts that require actual exit must track `onWorkerStarted(exited)` or retain capacity through `acquireWorker()`'s release callback

### Added

- Added `CodemodeSandbox`'s `onWorkerStarted(exited)` callback so hosts can count a worker against concurrency limits until it actually exits, independently of its script result
- Added `CodemodeSandbox`'s `acquireWorker()` hook to reserve shared capacity before starting a worker and release it only on actual exit or constructor failure

### Fixed

- Fixed aborts, timeouts, and `close()` waiting for worker termination on Bun while a non-interruptible built-in runs; shutdown now requests termination without waiting for exit ([#10748](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10748))

en.body:
### Added

- `SqliteStorage.open(database, { prefix })` can namespace every table and index; `openNodeSqliteStorage()` and `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage()` forward it, for databases shared with host tables.

### Changed

- Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite adapters created for the same storage object now coordinate their operations, allowing multiple Pi storages to safely share one Durable Object database.

### Fixed

- The system baseline written after a compaction now leads the model context when the kept history includes an assistant message, as does a first baseline written after earlier answers, instead of following the new input; Anthropic and OpenAI Codex requests sent it as a mid-conversation system message without an initial prompt or tool set. Other system messages after an assistant message stay in place ([#10904](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10904)).
- `toBase64`, used by `read` and the Photon image processor, no longer takes about 140 MB of heap to encode a 3 MiB image, which exceeded the 128 MB memory limit of a Cloudflare Durable Object; it now builds a binary string 8 KiB at a time and encodes it with `btoa` ([#10923](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10923)).

points.after: self.state、self.resource、self.on、self.derive、self.task 替换旧声明；状态版本与迁移归属各 cell。
points.why: 不能只改 import；重复名称、资源版本和监听器重建都有运行语义。
points.action: 对照当前 tutorial，迁移工厂与 reload 测试；旧 epoch 名称改 codeVersion，Handle 改 Ref。

points.title: 远程放置与身份变为显式契约
points.before: 调用者指定目标 host，宿主可能生成默认 principal。
points.after: remote 声明 hostNamed/hostFamily；createHost.self、connect.principal、upstream 的 link/principal 显式给出。
points.why: 放置参与契约指纹，身份来自应用；异版本链路不能随意互通。
points.action: 同时迁移消费端和提供端，await get 等初始状态就绪，检查 lifetime:host 与 awaitHostObjects。

points.title: 恢复会话保留已激活工具
points.before: 继续会话可能丢失运行时激活的工具。
points.after: 恢复保存集合，增减形式 --tools +name/-name 在其上应用；显式完整集合或禁用选项仍优先。
points.why: 恢复后的模型能力应对应已有会话选择。
points.action: 分别验证默认恢复、增减选择和明确覆盖，工作台原生设置不能偷偷重写既有会话选择。

points.title: 切换模型不把旧 reasoning 当普通回复
points.before: 上一模型 thinking 可能以可见文本传给新模型。
points.after: 来自其他模型的历史 thinking 块被丢弃。
points.why: 防止新模型把内部推理误学成可见回复格式。
points.action: 核对切换前后请求体与用户可见内容，保留其他历史消息。

points.title: 分享位置可配置
points.before: 分享上传位置由自动选择决定。
points.after: sessionShareDestination 可选 auto、gist、radius。
points.why: 导出本地文件与上传分享是不同操作。
points.action: 按组织要求选择目的地，阅读会话分享文档后显式执行。

points.title: 取消后的脚本 worker 纳入容量上限
points.before: 反复超时或取消可能累积尚未退出的 worker。
points.after: 限制跨会话同时存活 worker 为两个，取消后直到实际退出仍计数。
points.why: 取消通知不等于底层执行资源已释放。
points.action: 测试连续超时、取消与下一次启动，观察真实退出边界。

packages.description: 产品层：CLI、交互模式、扩展、模型运行时、会话与工具。学习主入口。

en.body:
### New Features

- **Per-key OpenRouter model lists**: with an OpenRouter key, Pi lists only the models that key may use, with the key's context size, max output, and prices, including regional endpoints set in `models.json`. See [OpenRouter](docs/providers.md#openrouter).
- **Published configuration schemas**: add `$schema` to `settings.json`, `models.json`, keybindings, and themes for editor validation and completion. See [Settings](docs/settings.md), [Models](docs/models.md), [Keybindings](docs/keybindings.md), and [Themes](docs/themes.md).
- **Clipboard copies over remote sessions**: `PI_CLIPBOARD_OSC52=1` sends copied text to a remote client's clipboard when Pi cannot detect the remote session, such as a multiplexer attached from another machine. See [Pi Process Configuration](docs/environment-variables.md#pi-process-configuration).
- **Codemode improvements**: tool declarations show input constraints such as integer, minimum/maximum, and default, and codemode rows show elapsed and total time. See [Codemode](docs/codemode.md).
- **`before_agent_start` for extension-triggered runs**: runs started by `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` go through the same setup as prompts. See [Events and concurrency](docs/extensions.md#events-and-concurrency).

### Breaking Changes

- Published generated configuration schemas for models, settings, keybindings, and themes at `https://pi.dev/schemas/*.schema.json`. The theme schema moved to `https://pi.dev/schemas/theme.schema.json`; themes loaded during startup now receive the same schema validation as later reloads. Update theme `$schema` references, define reusable colors under `vars`, and remove unsupported metadata ([#9880](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9880), [#10751](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10751) by [@christianklotz](https://github.com/christianklotz))
- Changed `before_agent_start` to also fire for runs started by `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` while idle. `BeforeAgentStartEvent` is now a union on `messageType`: `"user"` events carry `prompt` and `images`, and `"custom"` events carry the starting `message` and no `prompt`. Messages returned by handlers are added to both kinds of run, and pending `deliverAs: "nextTurn"` messages are delivered with the custom-message run. Handlers that should act only on user prompts must check `event.messageType === "user"` ([#10267](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10267), [#5581](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5581), [#10739](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10739) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Changed the session to count as busy while a run starts, including during `before_agent_start` handlers: `ctx.isIdle()` is false, `pi.sendMessage()` queues into the starting run instead of starting a second run that failed with "Agent is already processing", `pi.sendUserMessage()` requires `deliverAs`, and an abort requested meanwhile aborts the run once it starts ([#10739](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10739) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Changed `pi mcp list --json` to report `resources: true` for servers that offer resources instead of `resources` and `resourceTemplates` counts; Pi no longer lists resources when connecting ([#10526](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10526))

### Added

- Added `reachesTools` to tool definitions, so tools that reach other tools (such as `codemode` and `tool_search`) declare which tools a call may reach; the MCP extension uses it to wait for the servers a call needs and to decide whether a replacement `codemode` or `tool_search` tool can reach MCP tools
- Added `aliases` to tool namespaces; codemode's `describeNamespace()` and the `namespace` option of `searchTools()` match them, and MCP namespaces use the server name
- Added per-key OpenRouter model lists: with an OpenRouter key, Pi lists only the chat models that key may use, with the key's context size, max output, and prices, including guardrails and regional endpoints set as the base URL in `models.json`. The list is saved and used offline ([#10353](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10353), [#10672](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10672) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Added `PI_CLIPBOARD_OSC52=1` to send copied text to the terminal with OSC 52 after the local clipboard write, so copies reach a remote client's clipboard when Pi cannot detect the remote session, such as multiplexer attaches from another machine or remote IDE daemons ([#10826](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10826), [#10835](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10835), [#10114](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10114))
- Added elapsed time while a codemode script runs and its total time once finished to the codemode tool row, like bash rows ([#10708](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10708))

### Changed

- Changed the `showHardwareCursor` setting to use only the terminal cursor instead of also drawing Pi's reverse-video cursor
- Changed codemode tool declarations to show input constraints such as integer, minimum/maximum, length, pattern, and default as `@` tags on property comments, so scripts see them without the tool repeating them in descriptions ([#10707](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10707))
- Changed codemode declarations of MCP tools to spell out the result type (`content`, `structuredContent`, `isError`) instead of referring to `CallToolResult<T>`, which `describeTool()`, `searchTools()`, and `ALL_TOOLS` showed without defining it; the codemode description no longer includes the shared MCP types
- Changed `serializeConversation()` (compaction, branch summaries, bug reports) to omit thinking blocks; replayed thinking is often not in the live context, so including it could make a summarization request larger than the context it summarizes and fail

### Fixed

- Fixed codemode ignoring a `// @options:` line that is not the first line of the script, which ran the script without the requested `timeout_ms`; the call now fails with an error before the script runs ([#10631](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10631))
- Fixed Mistral streams being aborted mid-generation (e.g. during long thinking) after the request timeout; the timeout now applies only to waiting for response headers ([#10609](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10609))
- Fixed a symlinked `AGENTS.md` in a git worktree nested inside its main repo causing no project context file to load ([#10681](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10681))
- Fixed the code mode tool description claiming every failed tool call rejects; a tool that declares an output schema resolves with its value on failure too (e.g. `bash` with a nonzero exit)
- Fixed runs started by `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` removing system prompt sections added in `before_agent_start` after their first tool call, which changed the prompt mid-run and broke the provider prompt cache twice per run ([#10267](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10267), [#10739](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10739) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Fixed codemode blocking the process for seconds to minutes after scripts with many `text()` calls; joining the output items was quadratic ([#10678](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10678))
- Fixed print mode (`-p`) exiting 0 without a warning when the final response was cut off at the model's output token limit; it now prints the partial text, writes a warning to stderr, and exits 1 ([#10799](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10799))
- Fixed `pi mcp login --help` and the CLI docs describing `--timeout` as only the wait for the browser; it limits the whole sign-in ([#10636](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10636))
- Fixed `~` not being expanded in `!pattern`, `+path`, and `-path` entries of the `extensions`, `skills`, `prompts`, and `themes` settings, so entries like `!~/skills/pdf` matched nothing ([#10765](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10765))
- Fixed MCP servers with resources registering no tools until every resource was listed; Pi no longer lists resources when connecting, so `/mcp` and `pi mcp list` show that a server offers resources instead of counting them ([#10526](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10526))
- Fixed MCP tool calls failing when the server returns structured content that is not an object (an array, `null`, or a primitive, as MCP 2026-07-28 allows); codemode declarations of MCP tools without an output schema now type `structuredContent` as `unknown` instead of an object ([#10416](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10416))
- Fixed reading or writing `auth.json` on Windows failing with `EPERM` when the previous lock folder was still being deleted; Pi now retries briefly before reporting the error ([#10801](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10801))
- Fixed OpenRouter router models such as `openrouter/auto` showing a cost of -$1,000,000 per 1M tokens; OpenRouter's negative placeholder prices are now 0 ([#10672](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10672) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Fixed Anthropic requests failing when the provider rejects the strict tool set for grammar size, tool count, or union limits; Pi now retries once with preferred tools non-strict ([#10409](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10409))
- Fixed "The upstream provider returned an error" not being retried as a transient provider error ([#10842](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10842))
- Fixed focused fullscreen overlays blocking mouse-wheel scrolling of the transcript ([#10769](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10769))
- Fixed fragmented terminal color replies leaking hex values into the prompt and opening the external editor (related reports: [#10256](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10256), [#10657](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10657))
- Fixed inline images not rendering in Herdr since 1.1.0 ([#10774](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10774) by [@ogulcancelik](https://github.com/ogulcancelik))
- Fixed key bindings that name a shifted symbol, such as `+` or `ctrl++`, not matching under the Kitty keyboard protocol or modifyOtherKeys ([#9880](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9880) by [@christianklotz](https://github.com/christianklotz))
- Fixed the compaction status indicator embedded in a custom editor using the default muted colors instead of the editor border or thinking-level color, as the working indicator does ([#10809](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10809), [#10810](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10810) by [@Jay-Madden](https://github.com/Jay-Madden))
- Fixed MCP tool calls that were cancelled or timed out while waiting for an OAuth refresh still being sent to the server once the refresh finished ([#10598](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10598))
- Fixed MCP OAuth sign-in accepting an authorization response with an `iss` parameter that could not be checked because no authorization server metadata was discovered; sign-in now fails with an issuer mismatch. Reported by [@AizenvoltPrime](https://github.com/AizenvoltPrime)
- Fixed codemode failing with a broken bridge error when Pi runs under `node --watch` on Node 24 or 26 ([#10725](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10725))

### Removed

- Removed the unreleased experimental server, client, and plugin stack (`src/experimental`, `src/cli/experimental`) and its source-only `./client` and `./experimental/plugin` exports; none of it was part of the published package. The `@earendil-works/pi-client`, `@earendil-works/pi-protocol`, and `@earendil-works/pi-server` packages it used are removed and no longer released
- Removed the dependency on `@earendil-works/chord`

### Added

- Added `personalizeOpenRouterCatalog()` (`@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/openrouter`), which narrows an OpenRouter catalog to the chat models a key may use, with that key's context size, max output, and prices from `GET /models/user` ([#10353](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10353), [#10672](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10672) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Added `RefreshModelsContext.baseUrl`, the registered provider's base URL including configuration overrides applied by wrappers, so dynamic catalogs can follow a base URL set in `models.json` ([#10353](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10353), [#10672](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10672) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))

### Breaking Changes

- Replaced the facet and service runtime with a typed host runtime: contracts (`local`, `remote`, `method`, `opaque`) are runtime values described with TypeBox schemas, objects are served by hosts (`createHost`, `defineFacet`, `defineRegistry`) and reached through handles, and hosts exchange JSON frames over memory, Node IPC, or WebSocket links (`memoryLinkPair`, `ipcLink`, `webSocketLink`, `acceptWebSockets`), with hot reload of plugins. See `docs/tutorial.md` and `docs/guide.md`
- Removed `defineService`, `createFacetHost`, `createRemoteServiceBinding`, `createStaticFacetLoader`, `combineFacetLoaders`, the remote-service endpoint, provider, error, and wire helpers, and their types. The old `defineFacet`, `Facet`, and `FacetLoader` are replaced by the new runtime's names of the same spelling
- Removed the `./bundler` export and the facet bundle loaders of `./node`; `./node` now exports the child host manager (`createHostManager`, `forkDriver`, `childControl`, `processLock`) and the facet module loader `nodeLoader`
- Removed `@earendil-works/pi-client`, `@earendil-works/pi-protocol`, and `@earendil-works/pi-server`, which served only the old runtime; they are no longer released

### Changed

- `replicatedState`, `copyJson`, `isJsonValue`, `Context`, `JsonValue`, `JsonRepresentation`, `Draft`, and the replicated state types keep their names on the root export; `./context` and `./delta` are unchanged, and `./context` also exports the `Context` and `ContextKey` types
- Depends on `typebox` instead of `esbuild`

### Fixed

- Fixed appending to an array costing a walk over the whole array: the delta tracker now plans inserts and removals that keep the remaining elements in order from the changed ranges alone, and `applyImmutable` builds an appended array in one copy instead of two. 32,000 one-item appends, one commit each, take 1.4 s instead of 11.3 s
